title: Linkability of GPS coordinates to child identity
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted from child's device can be linked to the child's identity through the backend system, potentially enabling tracking of the child's movements and associations with other data.
assumptions: Backend maintains records linking GPS data to child identity

title: Identifiability through location patterns
description: Regular GPS transmissions reveal location patterns that can identify the child's home, school, and frequent locations, enabling inference of sensitive personal information.
assumptions: GPS data is transmitted at regular intervals over extended periods

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: Live GPS coordinates could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through backend system compromise, insecure transmission, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Backend system may have vulnerabilities or inadequate access controls

title: Excessive data collection via live GPS tracking
description: Continuous live GPS tracking may collect more location data than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Live continuous tracking is not the minimum necessary for the service purpose

title: Usurpation of GPS data transmission
description: Unauthorized individuals could potentially access the child's device and transmit false GPS coordinates, impersonating the child's location.
assumptions: Child's device may be accessible to unauthorized persons

title: Unintended Location Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Location pings written to the Location History Store may be accessible to unauthorized third parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or unauthorized API access, resulting in implicit disclosure of personal location data.
assumptions: The system lacks adequate access controls or the data store is accessible beyond intended recipients.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on context [5] about data disclosure; specific tree node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Linkability of Location History to Individual Identity
description: The stored location history can be linked to identify specific individuals over time, potentially revealing patterns of movement, routines, and associations that could be used to track or profile users.
assumptions: Location data is retained long enough to establish meaningful patterns and is not properly anonymized.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linkability threats; context [4] confirms L is applicable at Process→DataStore flows.

title: Identifiability of Location Data
description: Location pings contain personal data that can directly or indirectly identify individuals, especially when combined with timestamps and device identifiers.
assumptions: Location data is not sufficiently anonymized or pseudonymized before storage.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a reasonable node for identifiability threats; context [4] confirms I is applicable at Process→DataStore flows.

title: Unnecessary Location Data Disclosure to Geofencing Engine
description: Location pings containing personal location data are transferred from Mobile App Backend to Geofencing Engine. This disclosure may violate minimality principle if the geofencing engine could be implemented with less granular location data or if the transfer is not strictly necessary for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Location data contains personally identifiable information; the transfer is not the minimal necessary data for geofencing functionality.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on context [5] about data disclosure and minimality principle.

title: Location Data Used for Individual Identification
description: Location pings transferred to Geofencing Engine could be used to identify or track specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources. The transfer creates a pathway for identification that may not be necessary for geofencing functionality.
assumptions: Location data can be used to identify individuals; the geofencing engine may have access to additional identifying information.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 based on standard LINDDUN identification threat patterns.

title: Location Data Integrity Compromised During Transfer
description: Location pings transferred from Mobile App Backend to Geofencing Engine could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during the process-to-process transfer, leading to incorrect geofencing decisions or false alerts.
assumptions: The transfer mechanism is not fully secured against tampering; location data integrity is critical for accurate geofencing.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 based on standard LINDDUN data integrity threat patterns.

title: Linkability of Zone Definitions to Family Members
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) stored in DS2 can be linked to specific family members through the geofencing engine, potentially revealing which family member uses which location.
assumptions: Zone definitions are associated with specific family members in the system
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linkability threats in DataStore context

title: Identification of Family Members via Location Patterns
description: Zone definitions reveal where family members live, attend school, and visit friends, enabling identification of individuals through their location patterns and routines.
assumptions: Zone definitions are tied to specific family member accounts
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a reasonable node for identification threats in DataStore context

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Location Data
description: Zone definitions containing home addresses, school locations, and friend's house addresses could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if DS2 is compromised or accessed without proper authorization.
assumptions: Zone definitions are considered sensitive personal data
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable node for disclosure threats in DataStore context

title: Linkability of Geofencing Data to External Systems
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) could potentially link zone definition data to other data sources or external systems, creating a comprehensive profile of family members' movements and locations.
assumptions: P2 has access to or can communicate with other data sources
uncertainty_note: Using L.2.1 as a reasonable node for linkability threats in Process context

title: Inadvertent Disclosure During Geofencing Operations
description: The Geofencing Engine may inadvertently expose zone definition data through logs, error messages, or unintended data transmission during alert generation.
assumptions: P2 processes and potentially outputs zone definition data
uncertainty_note: Using D.2.1 as a reasonable node for disclosure threats in Process context

title: Linkability of Geofencing Notifications
description: The Geofencing Engine could emit multiple arrival/departure notifications that an external entity could link together to reconstruct the child's movement patterns and location history, potentially revealing sensitive behavioral information.
assumptions: External entity has access to notification stream and can correlate timestamps with location data
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 based on Process->ExternalEntity mapping; tree_node selection based on standard LINDDUN Pro threat tree structure

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Notifications
description: Arrival/departure notifications pushed to the external entity could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties, revealing the child's location and movement patterns to entities without legitimate access.
assumptions: Notification transmission channel lacks adequate access controls or encryption
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 based on Process->ExternalEntity mapping; severity elevated due to sensitive nature of child location data

title: Identification of Child's Location Patterns
description: The notification stream could enable identification of the child's routine movements, preferred locations, and behavioral patterns, potentially allowing inference of sensitive activities or locations.
assumptions: Notification metadata includes sufficient context to identify patterns
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 based on Process->ExternalEntity mapping; threat exists due to nature of geofencing tracking

title: Parent-Child Identity Linkability
description: The parent's identity can be linked to the child's profile data (name, DOB, school) and geofence zones, potentially enabling tracking of the child's activities through the parent's account.
assumptions: Parent account is used to manage child's data

title: Child Identification via Profile Data
description: Child's personally identifiable information (name, DOB, school) in the profile can be used to identify the child, potentially exposing them to privacy risks.
assumptions: Profile data is stored and accessible

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Personal Data
description: Child's sensitive information (name, DOB, school) and geofence zones could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through the registration process or data flow.
assumptions: Data is transmitted to backend system

title: Unauthorized Account Registration
description: An unauthorized third party could register an account and create a child's profile, potentially misrepresenting the child's identity or location preferences.
assumptions: Authentication controls may be insufficient

title: Non-compliance with Children's Privacy Regulations
description: The system may fail to comply with regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding collection and processing of children's personal data and location information.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements exist for child data

title: Excessive Personal Data Storage in Family Account Store
description: The backend (P1) stores comprehensive account, child profile, and geofence zone data in DS2. This raises concerns about data minimality - whether all stored data is strictly necessary for the intended functionality, or if some data could be collected/processed without compromising service quality.
assumptions: The system stores more data than minimally required for account management and geofencing functionality.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on context [3] about data disclosure and minimality principle

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Family Account Data
description: Personal data including child profiles and geofence zones stored in DS2 could be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient. This is particularly sensitive given the data involves minors' information.
assumptions: Access controls to DS2 may not be sufficiently restrictive, or there may be vulnerabilities in the authentication/authorization mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for usurpation threats

title: Data Integrity Risk for Child Profile Information
description: Child profile and geofence zone data stored in DS2 could be tampered with or corrupted, potentially leading to incorrect location tracking or inappropriate access permissions being granted.
assumptions: The system may lack adequate integrity controls, encryption, or audit mechanisms for the stored data.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for data integrity threats

title: Identifiability of Stored Family Account Data
description: The stored data (account information, child profiles, geofence zones) could potentially be used to identify specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources or through inference from geofence patterns.
assumptions: The data stored contains personally identifiable information that could be linked to specific individuals.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for identifiability threats

title: Unauthorized Location Data Disclosure
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) may disclose child's location or location history to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate access controls or encryption on location data
uncertainty_note: Citation D.1.1 from context is approximate for this specific flow

title: Child Identification via Location Data
description: Location data can be used to identify the child's identity, home address, school, or routine patterns, potentially revealing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Location data contains identifiable patterns or metadata
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as best judgement for identification threat

title: Location Data Usurpation
description: Unauthorized third parties may access or impersonate the child to view or manipulate location data through compromised credentials or system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be insufficient
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as best judgement for usurpation threat

title: GDPR/Privacy Regulation Non-Compliance
description: Processing child's location data may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other privacy regulations requiring parental consent and data minimization.
assumptions: Child is a minor and location data is special category data
uncertainty_note: Using Nc.1.1 as best judgement for compliance threat

title: Location History Linkability to Parent Identity
description: Stored location history data can be linked to the parent's identity through metadata, timestamps, or associated user accounts, enabling correlation with other data sources.
assumptions: Location history is stored with identifiable metadata or can be correlated with other data
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for linkability threats in LINDDUN Pro

title: Location History Enables Parent Identification
description: Location history data can directly identify the parent through unique movement patterns, frequently visited locations, or geotagged information.
assumptions: Location patterns are unique enough to identify individuals
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for identification threats in LINDDUN Pro

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location History
description: Location history data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data leaks, or unauthorized API access.
assumptions: Access controls may be insufficient or misconfigured
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for disclosure threats in LINDDUN Pro

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: The Mobile App Backend process could be compromised or accessed by unauthorized users, allowing them to retrieve and view the parent's location history.
assumptions: Process P1 may have insufficient authentication or authorization controls
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for usurpation threats in LINDDUN Pro

title: Parent identity linked with child location data
description: The parent's identity (as the inviter) could be linked with the child's location data being shared, creating a privacy risk where the parent's association with the child's location is exposed.
assumptions: The system records which parent initiated the guardian invitation and links this with the location data being shared.

title: Parent identifiable as location data sharer
description: The parent could be identified as the entity sharing the child's location data with the secondary guardian, potentially revealing the parent-child relationship.
assumptions: The system logs or displays the parent's identity when the location sharing invitation is processed.

title: Location data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The mobile app backend could disclose the child's location data to parties beyond the intended secondary guardian, such as through logging, analytics, or unintended data access.
assumptions: The process may have access to the location data and could potentially share it with other systems or parties.

title: Excessive location data retained
description: The mobile app backend may retain more location data than necessary for the secondary guardian viewing feature, including historical data or metadata beyond what's needed.
assumptions: The process stores location data for purposes beyond the immediate sharing function.

title: Location data accessed by unauthorized personnel
description: The mobile app backend could be compromised, allowing unauthorized personnel to access the child's location data that was shared via the parent's invitation.
assumptions: The process may have insufficient access controls or authentication mechanisms.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: Even though data is described as 'aggregated', there is a risk that usage and engagement patterns could be linked with other datasets (e.g., device IDs, IP addresses, or other partner data) to re-identify individual users or create detailed user profiles.
assumptions: Partner may have access to additional data sources that could be combined with this analytics data
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linkability threats in Process→ExternalEntity flows

title: Unauthorized Disclosure to Third Parties
description: The advertising/analytics partner may share or sell the received analytics data to additional third parties beyond the original scope of the partnership, potentially exposing user engagement patterns to unauthorized entities.
assumptions: Partner may have business incentives to monetize data beyond the agreed purpose
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 selected as appropriate node for disclosure threats in Process→ExternalEntity context

title: Excessive Data Collection and Sharing
description: The backend may be sharing more detailed usage and engagement data than necessary for the stated advertising/analytics purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The 'aggregated' description may not reflect actual data granularity being transmitted
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 chosen for data minimization concerns in Process→ExternalEntity flows

title: Unintended Data Usage by Partner
description: The advertising/analytics partner may use the received analytics data for purposes beyond the agreed-upon funding of the app's free tier, such as building user profiles for targeted advertising or selling to data brokers.
assumptions: Partner may have broader business objectives that conflict with the stated data-sharing purpose
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 selected for usability/usage concerns in Process→ExternalEntity context

title: Child's location data can identify the child
description: The manual check-in/SOS message contains the child's current location, which combined with the child's identity can be used to identify the child's whereabouts and potentially their identity to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The location data is precise enough to identify the child's location, and the message is accessible to parties who can link it to the child's identity.

title: Child's location data can be linked with other data sources
description: The location data in the check-in/SOS message can be linked with other data (e.g., parent's data, other check-ins, device identifiers) to create a more detailed profile of the child's movements and habits.
assumptions: Other data sources exist that can be correlated with this location data.

title: Child's location data can be disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The location information in the check-in/SOS message could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches.
assumptions: The system has access controls that may not be properly implemented or enforced.

title: Child's location data can be falsified or spoofed
description: The location data in the check-in/SOS message could be falsified or spoofed by the child or an attacker, leading to incorrect location information being processed.
assumptions: The child or an attacker has the capability to manipulate the location data before transmission.

title: Child's location data can be used to impersonate the child
description: The location data in the check-in/SOS message could be used by an attacker to impersonate the child, potentially gaining unauthorized access to parent-controlled features or services.
assumptions: The system relies on location data for authentication or authorization purposes.
